onboarding.welcomeBody: The app helps you track your mood and get quick support when you need it. Your data stays private.
onboarding.moodBody: Enter your daily mood (1–5). You can also keep a thought log: what you feel, what helps, place and situation – it helps you spot patterns later.
onboarding.sosBody: Breathing, grounding (5–4–3–2–1), mudras. You can add a safety plan with a contact and steps that help.
onboarding.plansBody: Daily rituals (e.g. 2 min breathing) and reminders to do them. Weekly review helps you see what helped.
onboarding.finishBody: The app is not a replacement for professional help. If you're struggling, reach out to a professional. When ready, start by entering today's mood.
onboarding.tryBreathBody: Tap the circle and follow one slow breath — inhale as it grows, exhale as it shrinks.
onboarding.tryBreathDone: Nice. You can use this anytime from Home.

breathing.title: Breathing
breathing.descPhysioSigh: Full inhale, then a short second inhale, then a long exhale (~10s per cycle). Fastest stress reset — even 1–3 rounds help.
breathing.descLongExhale: Inhale 4s → short hold 2s → exhale 6s (longer exhale calms)

mudras.title: Mudras
mudras.subtitle: Pick a mudra, read how to do it, then start a short practice.
mudras.doneGuidance: Well done. Notice how you feel and continue your day.
mudras.cueQuarter: Almost there. Soft grip, calm exhale.

gyan.title: Gyan mudra
gyan.summary: Classic meditation mudra: simple, stable, easy to focus with.
gyan.how: Touch the tip of thumb and index finger (no squeezing); other fingers relaxed and slightly extended. Palms can face up on your knees.
gyan.breath: Breathe slowly and quietly through the nose. Let the exhale be slightly longer than the inhale.
gyan.focus: On each exhale, relax shoulders and jaw.
gyan.mistake_0: Squeezing thumb and index too hard.
gyan.benefit_1: A good default for sitting and meditation.
gyan.caution: If fingers go numb or joints hurt, loosen the grip and change hand position.

prana.title: Prana mudra
prana.summary: When you feel "empty": a short practice for energy and alertness.
prana.how: Touch the tip of the thumb to the tips of the ring and little finger; index and middle finger stay extended and relaxed.
prana.breath: Inhale calmly for 4 seconds, exhale for 6 (no forcing).
prana.focus: Feel "filling" on the inhale, and release in the torso on the exhale.
prana.mistake_0: Forced deep breathing leading to dizziness.
prana.mistake_1: Squeezing the little or ring finger.
prana.benefit_0: Linked to vitality and reducing fatigue (traditional).
prana.benefit_1: Useful as a short break during the day.
prana.caution: If you feel dizzy, return to normal breathing and shorten the practice.

apana.title: Apana mudra
apana.summary: A calmer mudra, often linked to "downward" energy and a sense of release.
apana.how: Touch the tip of the thumb to the tips of the middle and ring finger; index and little finger stay extended and relaxed.
apana.breath: Breathe quietly and slowly, no holding. Focus on a soft, longer exhale.
apana.focus: On the exhale, "let go" so the belly softens (no pushing).
apana.mistake_0: Tensing the belly instead of relaxing.
apana.mistake_1: Too much pressure with the fingers.
apana.benefit_0: Traditionally linked to digestion and elimination.
apana.benefit_1: Can be a calming practice before sleep.
apana.caution: If you feel discomfort in belly or back, shorten the practice and sit more comfortably.

dhyana.title: Dhyana mudra
dhyana.summary: A stable sitting position: less fidgeting, more peace.
dhyana.how: Place your hands in your lap: right hand over left (or the other way), palms up; thumbs gently touching.
dhyana.breath: Breathe quietly through the nose. Let the exhale lengthen naturally.
dhyana.focus: Feel the weight of your hands in your lap and the steady rhythm of your breath.
dhyana.mistake_0: Pressing the thumbs together too hard.
dhyana.caution: If your back hurts, use a cushion or lean back; comfort comes first.

anjali.title: Anjali mudra
anjali.summary: Quick "reset" and centering—great at the start or end of practice.
anjali.how: Bring palms together in front of your chest (like "prayer"), elbows relaxed, shoulders down.
anjali.breath: 3–5 slow breaths in and out through the nose.
anjali.focus: On the exhale, soften the hands (don’t press the palms hard).
anjali.benefit_0: Gives a sense of center and brief calm.
anjali.benefit_1: Easy to use as a mini-ritual (start/stop).
anjali.caution: If your wrists hurt, lower the hands or relax the palms.

shuni.title: Shuni mudra
shuni.summary: When you want to slow down and stay grounded—without "revving up".
shuni.how: Touch the tip of the thumb to the tip of the middle finger; other fingers relaxed and slightly extended.
shuni.breath: Normal inhale, slightly longer exhale; no forcing.
shuni.benefit_1: Good when you’re nervous or scattered.

surya.title: Surya (Ravi) mudra
surya.summary: A short boost of alertness—when you need a bit of "drive".
surya.how: Bend the ring finger toward the palm and press it with the thumb; other fingers extended and relaxed.
surya.breath: Breathe normally or inhale 4 / exhale 6 (if it feels good).
surya.focus: Notice relaxing the grip after each exhale.
surya.mistake_0: Too much pressure of thumb on ring finger.
surya.benefit_1: Can feel good as a short break before work.
surya.caution: If you feel discomfort in the fingers, shorten or skip.

buddhi.title: Buddhi mudra
buddhi.summary: When you want clarity without strain—calm and simple.
buddhi.how: Touch the tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger; other fingers relaxed.
buddhi.breath: Calm breathing through the nose; exhale slightly longer.
buddhi.benefit_0: Often cited for mental clarity and calm focus (traditional).
